0x140b86b70.name: ImgAtex_Decode
0x140b86b70.comment:
Arena\Engine\Gr\Img\ImgAtex.cpp  ImgAtex_Decode - ATEX-family texture decoder.

HOW TO READ THIS FUNCTION
It is a RESUMABLE STATE MACHINE, not a straight-line decoder. The caller feeds it
bytes as they arrive off disk; each entry runs `switch (state)` (cases 0..13), consumes
what it can, saves progress back into `decoder`, and returns. `savedState`, `savedMipLevel`
and `savedBlockIndex` are the resume point. Partial words that straddle a chunk boundary
are parked in spillWord / spillBits / spillByteCount.

Flow:
  1. read 4-byte container magic  -> containerMagic (ATEX ATTX ATEC ATEP ATEU ATET)
  2. read 4-byte pixel fourCC     -> formatFourCC   -> grFormat (GR_FORMAT enum)
  3. read width and height        -> imageWidth / imageHeight
  4. for each mip level: read the per-mip flags, then run the fill passes

decoder-> FIELD MAP (offsets from the decoder pointer)
  +0x00  input pointer               +0x28  per-level output pointer array
  +0x08  input bytes available       +0x30  bytes consumed so far
  +0x0C  total file size             +0x38  image width
  +0x10  target platform             +0x3C  image height
  +0x44  grFormat (GR_FORMAT enum)   +0x58  detail (private decoder state)
  +0x4C  containerTag  <-- WRITE-ONLY, see note below
  +0x60  fileType (0=ATEX 1=DDS 2=other)
  +0x70..+0x7C  spill state for partial words across chunk boundaries
  +0x80  block width     +0x88  level byte size   +0x8C  blocks across
  +0x90  bits per pixel  +0x94  current mip level

fourCC -> GR_FORMAT (read straight off the switch in this function)
  DXT1=22 DXT2=23 DXT3=24 DXT4=25 DXT5=26 DXTA=27 DXTL=28 DXTN=29
  3DCX=30 BC5X=31 BC7X=32 ; uncompressed 11CU..39CU = 2..21 ; GR_FORMATS = 38

THE CONTAINER TAG IS WRITE-ONLY
containerTag (ATEC=1 ATEP=2 ATEU=4 ATET=0x20) is computed here and stored at +0x4C,
and that is the ONLY place it is ever touched. Nothing reads it back - not this
function, not the loaders, not the image allocator. So ATEP decodes byte-for-byte
identically to ATEX. There is no premultiplied-alpha step and no other
container-driven pixel transform. If a .atep looks wrong, suspect the VIEWER
ignoring alpha, not this decoder.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES THE PIXELS
Only two things: the pixel fourCC above, and the per-mip flags dword -
  0x1 / 0x2 / 0x4 / 0x8  gate the RLE constant-fill passes
  0x10                   256x256 terrain border mirror (ImgAtex_MirrorTerrainBorders)
  0x200                  no block bitmap, mip is stored raw

NOTE ON VARIABLE NAMES: the header-parse and per-mip state variables are named.
The ~245 short-lived register temporaries inside the fill passes are left as vNN -
they are single-use arithmetic scratch, and naming them would be guesswork.

0x140daae60.comment:
Key expansion: an 8-byte strs password -> the 20-byte key actually fed to RC4.
  (keyBytes, keyPtr, dstArray)
1. fill 20 bytes cyclically: dst[i] = key[i % keyBytes]
2. XOR in any key bytes past 20 (never happens for the 8-byte strs keys)
3. ONE SHA-1-shaped round over the 5 dwords, ROL5 / ROL30, constants
   -1615554381, 1722862861, 0x22222222, 0x7BF36AE2, -214083945,
   0x59D148C0, -696916869, -1269579175

  i = (i+1) & 255;  j = (j + S[i]) & 255;  swap(S[i], S[j]);
  out[n] = in[n] ^ S[(S[i] + S[j]) & 255]
RC4 IS SYMMETRIC, so this ONE function is both the encryptor and the decryptor - that is
why vtable slots 0 (encrypt) and 1 (decrypt) hold the same pointer. There is no separate
strs 'encrypt' routine to find.

0x1410dba40.name: TextDecode_DecodeRecord
0x1410dba40.comment:
TextDecode.cpp  the core record decoder - decrypt then bit-unpack.
  (decoder, textContext, stringId, record, key8)
Record header is u16[]: [0] = total length (>= 6), [1] = baseChar, byte[4] = rangeBits,
payload = record+3, payload length = record[0] - 6.

IF key8 != 0:  Cpt_ExpandKeyTo20(8, &key8) -> CptRc4_Create -> CptRc4_Crypt over the payload
ELSE:          the payload is copied verbatim

Then, if baseChar == 0 && rangeBits == 16 && the length is even, the payload IS raw UTF-16
and is passed straight through. Otherwise bit-unpack, LSB first, refilling while the
accumulator holds <= 0x18 bits:
    sym = acc & ((1 << rangeBits) - 1)
    sym == 0        -> NUL terminator
    sym in 1..31    -> TextDecode_SymbolTable[sym - 1]
    sym >= 0x20     -> (wchar)(sym + baseChar - 32)

strs file pulled straight out of Gw2.dat cannot be decrypted offline without captured keys.

0x141c80410.name: ImgFmt_Flags
0x141c80410.comment:
ImgFmt_Flags: dword[38] capability bits per GR_FORMAT.
  0x001  block compressed (4x4); drives ImgFmt_GetBlockDims
  0x210 / 0x280  select which PLANES a block carries. ImgAtex_Encode derives the block
         size from them:  planeDwords = (flags&0x280 ?2:0) + (flags&0x210 ?2:0)
                                      + (format==GR_FORMAT_DXTL ?2:0)
         and planeDwords*4 == bytes per block, cross-checked against bpp*16/8:
           DXT1 0x071 -> 0x210 only            ->  8 bytes  (1 colour block)
           DXTA 0x0a1 -> 0x280 only            ->  8 bytes  (1 alpha block)
           DXT2..5, BC7 0x0b1 -> both          -> 16 bytes  (alpha + colour)
           DXTN/3DC/BC5 0x201 -> both          -> 16 bytes  (two channels)
           DXTL 0x011 -> 0x210 + the DXTL case -> 16 bytes
This is why the ATEX container needs no per-format decoder: the flags tell it how many
8-byte planes a block has, and it moves blocks, never texels.

  [1] ALPHA bits       ARGB8888=8 ARGB4444=4 ARGB1555=1 RGB888=0 DXT1=1 DXT3/5=4
                       3DC/BC5/DXTN=0 (two-channel normal maps carry no alpha)
  [2] LUMINANCE bits   AL88=8 AL44=4 L8=8, zero for everything else
Read [0] via ImgFmt_GetBitCount. NOT a DXGI format map - the D3D11 format mapping lives
in BgfxTexture.cpp and was not traced.

inline_comments.0x140b86d97:
THE CONTAINER TAG IS WRITTEN HERE AND NEVER READ.
containerTag (ATEC=1 ATEP=2 ATEU=4 ATET=0x20) -> decoder+0x4C.
This is the ONLY access to +0x4C in the whole of ImgAtex_Decode, and it is a store.
Nothing loads it back, so the container magic cannot influence a single output pixel:
an .atep decodes byte-for-byte the same as an .atex.
inline_comments.0x140da2a98:
THE MAIN DECISION OF THE WHOLE DECOMPRESSOR.
symbol < 0x100  -> it is a plain byte, write it straight to the output.
symbol >= 0x100 -> it is a 'go back and repeat' instruction; the next steps read
                   how MANY bytes to repeat (length) and how FAR BACK to start
                   (distance), then copy that run forward.
inline_comments.0x140da2c9b:
Turn the distance symbol into an actual byte distance:
    distance = Cmp_DistBase[symbol] + (however many extra bits Cmp_DistExtraBits[symbol] says)
The copy then starts at outPtr - (distance + 1). Because the copy is byte-by-byte and
forward, a short distance deliberately repeats bytes it has only just written - that is
how long runs of the same pattern get compressed down to a few bits.
inline_comments.0x140da2da0:
The copy loop. Reads one byte at a time from outPtr-(distance+1) and appends it.
Overlapping on purpose: when distance is small the loop re-reads bytes it just wrote,
which is how a long repeated run is reproduced from a tiny code.
